articles.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
articles.summary: The world is going to need more default hard budget caps in the coming months and years. Agents greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code, but that costs money. Nobody wants to wake up to an over-budget bill generated by an agent overnight. Businesses don't want applications to throw errors because some budget was exceeded, but most will likely prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill. Hard budget caps should be the default - people who want to live dangerously should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis.

articles.title: When the Models Get Better, Your TAM Should Go Up
articles.summary: The first thing every AI native business needs to ensure is that their TAM goes up when models get better. Most AI businesses operate in the gap between what models can do and what the customer needs. Every model release eats a layer of that, and the market shrinks with it. If a better model is bad news for your business, you're arbitraging a capability gap on a timer.

articles.title: Salesforce, Atlassian, and HubSpot Are Starting to Charge for Agent API Access
articles.summary: SaaStr received an estimate of up to $240,000 a year for agent API access that had previously come with its software subscriptions. Its revenue agent makes 35,000 to 40,000 API calls a day across its tools. The agent proposed copying the data into a $5 Postgres database to reduce those calls, though SaaStr hasn't built that workaround yet. Salesforce is introducing access charges, and Atlassian already charges. HubSpot's fees appear limited to its own agents so far, with third-party agents still uncharged in SaaStr's account.

articles.title: Prediction: the next massive Google update is around the corner
articles.summary: Google updates its documentation with clues before launching major updates. The company rewrote its guidance on AI content this week. It is now 'critical' that sites manually fact-check and review all AI-generated content before publishing. Fake authors are now categorized as a form of deception. Google has now announced what it considers low quality - now is the time to fix any issues before the update officially rolls out.

articles.title: When Are Negative Gross Margins Acceptable for an AI Startup?
articles.summary: Your AI product gets better, customers use it more, and each account becomes less profitable. Harvey reportedly hit negative 50% gross margins in June as usage grew under flat seat pricing. Subsidizing usage can help acquire customers or learn what they'll pay for, but it needs a way out. The comparison with Legora lays out three options. Charge for usage, make each request cheaper, or cap what's included. One proposed test is whether customers would stay when the product keeps 40 cents of each dollar after covering the cost of serving them.

articles.title: Is Buying Your Product Optional for the Customers You Are Targeting?
articles.summary: Your best customer loves the product. Why won't another company just like them buy it? Having the same problem doesn't mean having the same reason to act now. Take AI search. A marketer might urgently need a dashboard because their boss wants an answer about visibility, while feeling little pressure to buy a tool that actually improves it. Look back at what was happening when customers bought. What could they no longer postpone, and why couldn't their existing tools or another available option solve it?

articles.title: Cloudflare Birthday Week 2026 (Website)
articles.summary: Cloudflare made a series of announcements during its birthday week last week. This page puts them all in one place. The entries are ordered by announcement day. The announcements include new releases, security tools, monetization programs, and agent harnesses.

articles.title: Supabase Select 2026 Recap
articles.summary: Supabase now works code-first. Developers can build anything because the agent works in the same code they do. The agent can find problems, and the developer decides what to merge, so they can operate with confidence. Apps can scale without limits as the same Postgres carries it from prototype to petabyte.

articles.title: Exited Founders in San Francisco Are Renting a $4 Million Midlife Hacker House
articles.summary: One founder sold his company in 2021 and now flies from Austin to San Francisco every other week to be near the AI scene. He's staying at Vibe House SF, a $4 million house aimed at founders who've already had an exit. Stays last up to two weeks, and the house hosts events three times a week. Alongside the demos and dinners are $140 grounding sheets, quartz singing bowls, and a 3,300-word manifesto.

articles.title: The Cognition Playbook: From Debunked Demo to $1B ARR
articles.summary: Cognition crossed $1 billion in annualized revenue on September 25. It was at $1 million just 24 months earlier. The company had no customers and no revenue when its launch video went viral in March 2024. Since then, the company has raised three rounds in the last twelve months, the last one at $48 billion, and bought Windsurf, a company five times its size. The company's own agent now writes about 90% of its code.

articles.title: A Founder Got to $120K in Revenue by DMing People Who Had Already Complained About the Problem
articles.summary: A founder reporting $120K ARR says his first 100 users came from direct conversations.

articles.title: A Podcast Data Startup Was Bought by the Customer Already Running on Its Technology
articles.summary: Audiohook bought Podscan after building its own product on Podscan's podcast data.

articles.title: Your Country Needs Builders
articles.summary: We underestimate how much can change when people are given the means to build useful things.

articles.title: Final Companies: The End State of AI Agents
articles.summary: AI agents could become the primary gateway to commerce and online activity, controlling which businesses receive traffic and spending.
